summary: Milestone 2026.07.509 completed 12 experiments in 216.9 minutes, including 4 compute-bound tasks. The slowest recorded task was compute-bound at 63.18 minutes, while the locked task-conditioned indicator reports no GPU-idle condition on compute-bound work.
bottlenecks_identified: The 63.18-minute transition and retirement-map task and the 24.4-minute ARC transition-hypothesis prototype were the longest visible compute-bound paths; the supplied data does not provide phase-level causes for either duration.

The 36.88-minute reconciliation, 35.57-minute independent audit, and 24.82-minute shadow integration were long synthesis-only paths; their lack of GPU use is expected, so GPU scheduling is not identified as their bottleneck.
Disk-mtime reconstruction supplies experiment-level elapsed time without task-correlated GPU or loaded-model concurrency records, preventing causal and runner-selection attribution.
improvements_suggested: Generate a schema-validated dependency and retirement-map scaffold from prior terminal evidence before the transition task begins.
Emit phase-level timing receipts and task-scoped GPU telemetry for every compute-bound experiment.
Record loaded-model concurrency and selected runner in each compute-bound receipt, selecting DualGPURunner only when at least 2 models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Prebuild and validate the dependency and retirement-map scaffold for the next transition.
Add phase-level timing and task-correlated GPU utilization to compute-bound receipts.
Add explicit model-concurrency and runner-selection fields, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The evidence ranks elapsed paths but does not explain why they were slow or correlate the GPU snapshot with task windows. A nonzero time-savings estimate is not defensible until phase and concurrency telemetry provide a measured counterfactual.
